lessons.name: Poppy Station
lessons.summary: Poppy Station is a French association that develops and preserves the open-source Poppy robot ecosystem for education, research and the arts.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Poppy Station is a French association that develops and preserves the open-source Poppy robot ecosystem for education, research and the arts.

![An open-source, 3D-printed Poppy humanoid robot](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-poppy-station.webp)
*An open-source, 3D-printed Poppy humanoid robot. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Open-Source_3D_printed_Poppy_humanoid_robot.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Poppy Station took over the Poppy ecosystem** that Inria transferred to an external multi-partner structure.
- **The ecosystem bundles hardware and software** to build and program robots, plus teaching content and an interdisciplinary community.
- **Poppy Humanoid** is an open-source, 3D-printed humanoid aimed at research and education.
- **Poppy Ergo Jr** is a modular, 3D-printed arm that uses low-cost XL-320 motors.
- **The pypot library** is the project's Python library for controlling Dynamixel motors.

> **Key idea:** Poppy shows that a robot can be an open project: printable parts, public code and shared lessons.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Python first:** pypot lets a software student command real motors without writing firmware.
- **Open designs** let you see how printed parts, smart servos and a single-board computer fit together.
- On the map, Poppy Station links to **Poppy robots (Poppy Humanoid / Ergo Jr)**, a cheap comparison point for SO-101-style arms.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the humanoid overview** to see the robot's parts and motion.
2. **Read the Ergo Jr and pypot repositories** and note which motors, boards and libraries they use.
3. **Use the contact form** on the Poppy Station site for education or member questions; check activity dates before relying on any repository.

lessons.name: Post Tenebras Lab
lessons.summary: Post Tenebras Lab is a nonprofit Geneva hackerspace in Carouge where members share electronics, wood and metal workshops, tools and know-how.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Post Tenebras Lab is a nonprofit Geneva hackerspace in Carouge where members share electronics, wood and metal workshops, tools and know-how.

![The CNC machine's new touchscreen laptop at Post Tenebras Lab](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-post-tenebras-lab.webp)
*The CNC machine's new touchscreen laptop at Post Tenebras Lab. Source: [Post Tenebras Lab blog](https://www.posttenebraslab.ch/wiki/blog/2024/0328_new_stuff_2024), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Founded in 2009**, the association offers space, tools and technical culture for building, modifying and sharing objects.
- **Three workshops** cover electronics, wood and metal, plus a shared space and kitchen.
- **Equipment includes** 3D printers, a CNC machine, soldering irons, oscilloscopes, servers and computers.
- **Members document projects** on a public wiki, from the PTL-cyclone CNC to an ESPHome-controlled HDMI switch.

> **Key idea:** A hackerspace gives you the tools a dorm room lacks: soldering, printing, machining and people to ask.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Hardware practice:** robots need soldered wiring, printed brackets and measured signals, which these workshops support.
- **Oscilloscopes** let you see motor and sensor signals instead of guessing from software logs.
- **The public wiki** shows how members write up builds, a habit worth copying for lab projects.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the presentation video** to see the space before visiting.
2. **Check the calendar**, then join the open Tuesday-evening member session; non-members should contact the committee first.
3. **Read the wiki tutorials and project pages** to find people who have used the CNC or 3D printers.

lessons.name: Projet & Tech' (Télécom Saint-Étienne)
lessons.summary: Projet & Tech' is Télécom Saint-Étienne's student robotics association, which has entered the French robotics cup every year since 1995.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Projet & Tech' is Télécom Saint-Étienne's student robotics association, which has entered the French robotics cup every year since 1995.

![Students pictured on Télécom Saint-Étienne's Projet & Tech page](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-projet-tech.webp)
*Students pictured on Télécom Saint-Étienne's Projet & Tech page. Source: [Télécom Saint-Étienne](https://www.telecom-st-etienne.fr/ecole/associations-etudiantes/projet-et-tech/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Each season the team builds a main robot** plus small auxiliary robots called **PAMIs** for the Coupe de France de Robotique.
- **Skills covered** include 3D-printed parts, embedded programming, electronic boards and camera-based obstacle detection.
- **Regular workshops** teach PAMI building, 3D modelling, printing and laser cutting at the university FabLab.
- **Its YouTube channel** archives matches from the Coupe de France and the Coupe de Suisse.

> **Key idea:** A competition club turns a yearly rulebook into a deadline: design, build, test, then play real matches.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Same contest, same constraints:** the cup is the obvious first competition for a French student robotics team.
- **PAMIs are small robots**, a manageable scale for a first embedded and mechanical project.
- **Alumni support** is part of the model; a new lab can borrow this mentoring habit.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2016 cup video** to see a full match robot in action.
2. **Read the association page** for the skills and workshops it lists.
3. **Look for its team** in Coupe de France lists and matches, and talk to members there.

lessons.name: Proxinnov
lessons.summary: Proxinnov is a French industrial-robotics technology resource centre in La Roche-sur-Yon that helps manufacturers test, prototype and adopt robot cells.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Proxinnov is a French industrial-robotics technology resource centre in La Roche-sur-Yon that helps manufacturers test, prototype and adopt robot cells.

![Overview of Proxinnov's Usine Pilote robotised pilot factory](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-proxinnov.webp)
*Overview of Proxinnov's Usine Pilote robotised pilot factory. Source: [Proxinnov](https://www.proxinnov.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **It runs the industrial-robotics network** and supports manufacturers with Industry 4.0 projects, from awareness to studies and experiments.
- **The Usine Pilote** at its La Roche-sur-Yon headquarters holds about fifteen robot cells, each showing one application such as machining, welding or logistics.
- **With the Tech Lab**, these spaces total 1,200 m² for training, tests, trials and prototyping.
- **It joins research projects** such as Amatsumara, which aims to automate pre-weld assembly of long, heavy metal parts.

> **Key idea:** Industry tests a robot cell before buying it; a pilot factory is where that test happens.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Real factory tasks:** welding, finishing and cobot cells show what industrial robots are actually used for.
- **Software-heavy problems** such as vision and safety appear on its list of technologies demonstrated in the pilot factory.
- **Webinars and events** are a low-cost way to learn how manufacturers judge a robot project.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a RDV Tech recap** to see the kind of plug-and-play robotics topics it covers.
2. **Read the Usine Pilote page** and list which cells match a software or vision project idea.
3. **Check the events page** for public webinars and meetings before contacting the team.

lessons.name: RCVA
lessons.summary: RCVA (Robot Concept Ville d'Avray) is a French student robotics team that builds autonomous robots for the Coupe de France and Eurobot.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RCVA (Robot Concept Ville d'Avray) is a French student robotics team that builds autonomous robots for the Coupe de France and Eurobot.

![3D render of the 2026 Coupe de France table, theme Winter is coming](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-rcva.webp)
*3D render of the 2026 Coupe de France table, theme Winter is coming. Source: [RCVA, Winter is coming 2026](https://www.rcva.fr/winter-is-coming-2026/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The team has about ten students** from the GEII department of IUT de Ville d'Avray, plus alumni who already competed.
- **Everything is home-made:** mechanics in the team workshop, electronic boards sized to the mechanics, software rewritten for each year's rules.
- **Its record lists** French champion in 2026 and French and European champion in 2023, 2017 and 2015.
- **It publishes courses** on movement, motor control (asservissement) and localisation, plus course videos.

> **Key idea:** Winning teams master the basics: knowing where the robot is and making it follow a path exactly.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Free control lessons:** the asservissement course explains trajectory following with odometry and incremental encoders, the core of any mobile robot.
- **Software meets physics:** the team adapts its code every year, a clear model for a software-first lab.
- **A strong benchmark** for what a small student team can reach in this competition.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the team trailer** and a match video to see robot speed and precision.
2. **Work through the asservissement and localisation courses** before writing your own motor controller.
3. **Compare your robot design** with RCVA's season pages and talk to the team at the Coupe de France.

lessons.name: RoboCup France
lessons.summary: RoboCup France is the national committee that runs RoboCup Junior in France and links French teams to the international RoboCup leagues.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RoboCup France is the national committee that runs RoboCup Junior in France and links French teams to the international RoboCup leagues.

![RoboCup France logo](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robocup-france.webp)
*RoboCup France logo. Source: [RoboCup France](https://www.robocup.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **RoboCup describes itself** as the largest international robotics and AI competition, aiming for humanoids to beat the football world champions by 2050.
- **Leagues cover** football, rescue, domestic (@Home) and industrial robotics; France hosted the world event in 1998 (Paris) and 2023 (Bordeaux).
- **The French committee** selects Junior and Soccer Cam Track teams for European and world events; FFROB runs the Junior national final.
- **Major teams** apply to international events through each league's executive committee.

> **Key idea:** RoboCup turns open research problems into yearly matches with shared rules, so progress is easy to compare.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Major leagues need software:** RoboCup@Home, Rescue simulation and humanoid football mostly test perception, planning and learning.
- **Mentoring Junior teams** is a concrete outreach role for a university lab.
- **Rules change:** in July 2025 the trustees refocused football leagues on humanoids and dropped the non-humanoid ones.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the RoboCup Junior 2024 Bordeaux video** to see the event and robots.
2. **Read the league list** and pick one whose rules match your team's skills.
3. **Use the contact page or the RoboCupJunior mailing list, Discord and forum** before applying or volunteering.

lessons.name: Robopoly
lessons.summary: Robopoly is EPFL's student-run makerspace in Lausanne, where beginners and experienced makers build electronics, mechanics and robotics projects.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robopoly is EPFL's student-run makerspace in Lausanne, where beginners and experienced makers build electronics, mechanics and robotics projects.

![A Robopoly member designing a part in CAD software](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robopoly.webp)
*A Robopoly member designing a part in CAD software. Source: [Robopoly, EPFL](https://www.epfl.ch/campus/associations/robopoly/en/robopoly-4/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Members from EPFL or other schools** use a workshop full of tools, machines and components, with advice from the committee.
- **Membership costs CHF 5** and gives 24/7 access until the next academic year, plus workshops and drop-in sessions.
- **No prior knowledge is required**; drop-in sessions run every Monday from 17:00 to 19:00 in room BM9139.
- **Its GitHub hosts 64 repositories**, including the PRismino robotics platform, a self-balancing PIDPOD and an OpenCV SCARA image drawer.

> **Key idea:** A makerspace lowers the cost of a first hardware mistake: tools, parts and advice are in one room.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A model for a student lab:** a cheap membership, open hours and mentors make hardware accessible to software students.
- **Real code examples:** the SCARA drawer joins computer vision and arm control, a natural 42 bridge project.
- **Swiss network:** Robopoly appears at Swiss Robotics Industry Day, a place to meet Swiss robotics companies.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Swiss Robotics Industry Day interview** to hear how members describe the club.
2. **Browse the GitHub organisation** and read one small project end to end, such as PIDPOD.
3. **When in Lausanne, join a Monday drop-in session** or ask for a guided tour without registering.

lessons.name: RobotESEO
lessons.summary: RobotESEO is the ESEO engineering school's robotics club in Angers, designing autonomous robots for the Coupe de France de robotique since 1995.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RobotESEO is the ESEO engineering school's robotics club in Angers, designing autonomous robots for the Coupe de France de robotique since 1995.

![A RobotESEO robot on the Coupe de France table](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-roboteseo.webp)
*A RobotESEO robot on the Coupe de France table. Source: [RobotESEO](https://robot-eseo.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Students design, machine and program** their robots; on cup day each robot plays **100 seconds** alone, avoiding its opponent.
- **Five teams share the work:** mechanics, electronics, software, communication and a board that handles budget and handover between student years.
- **Its record lists** French titles in 1997, 2022 and 2024.
- **In 2026 it topped qualifying** among about a hundred teams, with a record 202 points, after rewriting its software and main electronics.

> **Key idea:** A cup robot must sense, decide and move with nobody at the controls, so software makes or breaks the season.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Clear software scope:** its software team covers match strategy, motor control, obstacle avoidance and vision.
- **Handover matters:** a board that passes knowledge between student cohorts is a useful pattern for a lab with yearly turnover.
- **A rewrite can pay off:** the 2026 software and electronics overhaul preceded its best qualifying score.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2026 cup video** and one 2025 match to see autonomous play.
2. **Read the club and seasons pages** to see how rules and robots change every year.
3. **Meet the team at the Coupe de France**, or use the contact page for technical exchange.

lessons.name: Robotics Place
lessons.summary: Robotics Place is an Occitanie robotics cluster, created in 2012, that brings together regional robotics companies, research labs and schools.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Place is an Occitanie robotics cluster, created in 2012, that brings together regional robotics companies, research labs and schools.

![An exhibition hall at a Robotics Place event](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robotics-place.webp)
*An exhibition hall at a Robotics Place event. Source: [Robotics Place, L'association](https://www.robotics-place.com/lassociation/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Founded by regional robotics companies**, the cluster helps them pool resources and share expertise.
- **The cluster runs collaborative R&D**, coordinates tender responses and links competing firms, an approach it calls **coopétition**.
- **Core topics** are Industry of the Future: production robots and cobots, AGV and AMR mobile robots, 3D printing, predictive maintenance, AR/VR and IoT sensors.
- **Its missions** also cover export, international partners, ethics and user acceptance of robots.

> **Key idea:** A cluster is a matchmaker: it connects a robotics problem with the regional experts who can solve it.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Industry map:** its member directory shows which robot makers and integrators work outside Paris.
- **Mobile robots** for supplying production lines are a field where navigation and perception software matter.
- **Ethics and acceptance** are on its agenda, useful context for any demo involving people.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Robotics Place DAY 2024 film** to see the event format and members.
2. **Read the missions page** and the member directory before proposing a joint project.
3. **Check the events page** for public cluster days, then use the contact form for specific questions.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Valley is a Dijon-based cluster, created in 2018, that promotes robotics and Industry 4.0 across Bourgogne-Franche-Comté.

![An industrial robot arm shown on the Robotics Valley cluster page](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robotics-valley.webp)
*An industrial robot arm shown on the Robotics Valley cluster page. Source: [Robotics Valley, Le cluster](https://www.robotics-valley.eu/presentation/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The association was created in 2018** with support from Dijon Métropole, the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region and the UIMM industry innovation fund.
- **Its mission** is to connect regional actors, support R&D and help companies enter emerging markets.
- **It can run feasibility studies** for robotics and Industry 4.0 projects, using its own staff or partner network.
- **Events include** an Industry 4.0 club with UIMM Côte-d'Or, technical days, working groups, webinars and lab-industry meetings.

> **Key idea:** Regional clusters show where robots are actually being bought and deployed, not only researched.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Industry problems:** club topics include process automation, no-code tools and AI uses in industry.
- **Webinar replays** on its YouTube channel are free and show how vendors pitch robot solutions to factories.
- **A map outside Paris** helps a student lab find partners for real-world test cases.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the cluster's membership video** to understand what members expect.
2. **Watch one webinar replay**, such as the Inbolt session, and note the technical problem it solves.
3. **Check the agenda** for public technical days before contacting the cluster.

lessons.name: Robotech Nancy (Polytech Nancy)
lessons.summary: Robotech Nancy is Polytech Nancy’s student team building autonomous robots for the Coupe de France de Robotique.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotech Nancy is Polytech Nancy’s student team building autonomous robots for the Coupe de France de Robotique.

![Robotech Nancy’s large robot for the 2022 competition](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robotech-nancy.webp)
*Robotech Nancy’s large robot for the 2022 competition. Source: [Robotech Nancy (Polytech Nancy)](https://robotech.polytech-nancy.univ-lorraine.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Autonomous robots** execute tasks without somebody steering them; the team combines mechanical design, electronics and programming to make that possible.
- **Two collaborating robots** were the 2022 design: they exchanged mission progress over radio and changed strategy when one robot encountered trouble.
- **Independent functional blocks** structure the project, alongside graph-based software and web interfaces for interacting with the robots.

> **Key idea:** Cooperation needs explicit messages about progress and failure, not just two robots running the same script.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think distributed systems:** each robot resembles a service; coordination depends on messages arriving with useful state, not on shared assumptions.
- **A concrete reading exercise:** trace “robot A cannot finish” into a new task for robot B in the 2022 account.
- **Compare Robotronik (Grenoble INP Phelma)** for another student route into the same competition, rather than assuming cup robots require machine learning.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2022 team video** before reading the technical description; identify the two machines and the tasks they attempt.
2. **Browse the public GitHub** for its maintenance interface and communication repositories; distinguish diagnostic tools from on-robot code.
3. **Use the team website** to ask a focused question about inter-robot communication or knowledge handover between student cohorts.

lessons.name: Robotium (ECAM-EPMI)
lessons.summary: Robotium is ECAM-EPMI’s robotics association, where students build competition robots and creative projects such as a full-size R2-D2.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotium is ECAM-EPMI’s robotics association, where students build competition robots and creative projects such as a full-size R2-D2.

![Robotium’s R2-D2 replica](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robotium.webp)
*Robotium’s R2-D2 replica. Source: [Robotium (ECAM-EPMI)](https://www.robotium.ecamepmi.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Several project groups** work on robots, drones, electronics and 3D-printed parts; the association explicitly welcomes beginners without prior technical knowledge.
- **The competition project** builds an autonomous robot, meaning a machine that acts without a person steering it during the match.
- **The R2-D2 build log** joins programming, mechanics and electronics; its early foot-drive design targeted roughly 40 kg on three feet, two motorized.

> **Key idea:** A friendly-looking robot still needs a written specification linking software behavior to mechanical limits.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Start from requirements:** the R2-D2 account considers balance, motor dimensions and slopes before choosing and modelling the feet.
- **Think API contracts:** a motor command is only useful when both the code and the physical mechanism agree on what it can deliver.
- **Compare SiERA (ESTACA)** as another student association with an R2-D2 project; a familiar character can make engineering easier to explain publicly.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the school’s Robotium introduction** to recognize the association before exploring its project archive.
2. **Read one R2-D2 subsystem** and list its inputs, mechanical constraints and expected behavior; do not treat old budgets as current prices.
3. **Use the association website’s public contact** to propose a small exchange about beginner onboarding or documenting an unfinished build.

lessons.summary: Robotronik is Grenoble INP Phelma’s electronics and robotics club, combining autonomous-robot competitions, personal projects and a repair service.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotronik is Grenoble INP Phelma’s electronics and robotics club, combining autonomous-robot competitions, personal projects and a repair service.

![Robotronik’s red competition robot in 2024](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-robotronik.webp)
*Robotronik’s red competition robot in 2024. Source: [Robotronik (Grenoble INP Phelma)](https://robotronik.fr/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two competition routes** appear on the club site: the Coupe de France de Robotique and NXP Cup, a race for autonomous cars.
- **The workshop supports projects** with 3D printers, programmable boards and tutoring in electronics and computing, alongside a Repair Corner for Phelma’s community.
- **The 2026 cup result** was third place among 108 teams; the club reports 579 qualification points and a 126–68 small-final win.

> **Key idea:** The competition robot, workshop and repair bench reinforce the same habit: diagnose a physical system, change it, and test again.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A useful software bridge:** the public repositories include motor-position control and a Jetson CAN-interface library; CAN is a bus for exchanging messages between devices.
- **Think integration tests:** a correct motion function is not enough if motor wiring, timing or the mechanism fails when everything runs together.
- **Compare Robotech Nancy (Polytech Nancy)** for a different organization of the same yearly competition challenge.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the club introduction** and identify which activity interests your team: competition, electronics projects or repairs.
2. **Browse one public repository** and map its hardware assumptions before attempting to reuse code.
3. **Use the club’s public partnership contact** to suggest a focused technical exchange, with one concrete question and a small demo.

lessons.summary: Roboy is a humanoid robotics project whose muscle-and-tendon robots and student-team history now continue through Robodies.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Roboy is a humanoid robotics project whose muscle-and-tendon robots and student-team history now continue through Robodies.

![Roboy 3.0 reaching toward cups at its unveiling](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-roboy.webp)
*Roboy 3.0 reaching toward cups at its unveiling. Source: [Roboy](https://roboy.org/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Musculoskeletal robots** imitate muscles and tendons rather than only placing motors directly at joints; this is the project’s central design idea.
- **Roboy 3.0** combines a humanoid body with an operator interface called the Teleportal; telepresence means acting remotely through the robot.
- **Its technical page lists** custom muscle units providing 300 N of force and a PyBullet simulation model for testing before hardware.
- **The organization evolved** from a student team into a not-for-profit research company; its homepage now announces Robodies and says the Roboy archive will not be updated.

> **Key idea:** The robot body and the remote operator interface are two halves of one system.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think client and server:** the operator interface sends intent, while the physical robot must turn it into achievable motion.
- **Roboy 3.0 is a related map node:** use its historical design to compare bio-inspired mechanisms with the simpler SO-101 arm.
- **A practical reading exercise:** separate the simulator, communication messages and physical muscle units in a sketch of the system.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the successor’s robot demonstration** to connect the archive’s telepresence idea with visible action.
2. **Inspect the public Roboy repositories** for simulation and communication code; check each project’s age and documentation before reuse.
3. **Follow the homepage’s Robodies transition link** for current engagement rather than assuming archived student programs remain open.

> **Key idea:** A student AI community can connect papers, prototypes and public demos without making every project a robot.

- **A useful organizational comparison:** 42AI can study how separate research, projects and events tracks support one community instead of competing for every member’s attention.
- **Think modular architecture:** give a robotics task force a clear interface to the wider association, such as a reproducible demo and short technical write-up.
- **Try a small planning exercise:** outline one arm-grasp experiment, one measurable success criterion and one public presentation, rather than promising a general-purpose robot.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the community interview** for an introduction to how TUM.ai connects research, industry and innovation; the discussion is in German.
2. **Read the research page** to distinguish a student task force from a dedicated robotics laboratory.
3. **Check the public events calendar** and contact the initiative with a specific peer-project or workshop proposal, not an assumption of shared equipment.

## In one sentence

- **Autonomous robots** act without a driver during the match; the school’s 2014 account describes collecting fruit and capturing model mammoths.

> **Key idea:** A competition rulebook turns a broad ambition into specific behaviors you can implement and test.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think executable specifications:** “collect a fruit” becomes approach, align, grip and return; each transition needs an observable success condition.
- **Practice integration:** the 2014 students describe intensive final testing, showing why programming cannot be separated from the mechanism it controls.
- **Compare Robotech Nancy (Polytech Nancy)** for another school team; these Montpellier sources are historical, not evidence of today’s equipment or membership.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2013 match** and identify one attempted action, one obstacle and one recovery opportunity.
2. **Read the 2014 school report** and turn one game task into a short checklist of acceptance tests.
3. **Approach Polytech Montpellier through public school channels** to check the team’s present activity before proposing an exchange; these archives do not establish current access.

lessons.summary: VRAC is a robotics team whose public Eurobot tools help builders simulate competition robots, inspect signals and share reusable engineering resources.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

VRAC is a robotics team whose public Eurobot tools help builders simulate competition robots, inspect signals and share reusable engineering resources.

![VRAC’s Webots simulation of a Eurobot table with robots](/img/lessons/orgs_association_3-vrac.webp)
*VRAC’s Webots simulation of a Eurobot table with robots. Source: [VRAC (ARDIC – IUT Cachan alumni)](https://github.com/VRAC-team/webots_eurobot_example), MIT.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A public simulation example** uses Webots, a program that models robots and their surroundings, with concise Python controllers.
- **Two drive designs** are provided: two powered wheels for a differential-drive robot, and four special omni wheels for sideways-capable motion.
- **A 10 ms simulation step** means the model advances one hundred times per simulated second; the README explicitly warns that simulated physics are imperfect.

> **Key idea:** Simulation lets software and mechanical work proceed together, but a successful virtual run is not proof that the real machine works.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think test doubles:** a simulated motor stands in for hardware, letting you exercise strategy before the physical robot is available.
- **Inspect the interface:** the example connects robot programs through virtual CAN, a software version of the message bus used between embedded devices.
- **Compare Robotech Nancy (Polytech Nancy)** for real competition coordination; VRAC’s shared tools offer a practical way to rehearse similar integration problems.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the assembly video** to connect the software example with a physical competition build.
2. **Open the simulation README** and trace keyboard input to wheel movement before attempting the external-controller example.
3. **Browse the resource collection** and report a reproducible documentation issue through the public repository, including your platform and the exact failing step.

- **A concrete reading exercise:** find where a received measurement becomes a colored display or graph; separate raw values from presentation logic.

2. **Read the ControlPanel disclaimer**: it is an implementation example for the team’s prototypes, not a supported universal framework.

Silicon Valley Robotics is a nonprofit industry association connecting robotics companies, researchers and builders through events and commercialization support.

- **An ecosystem connector**, rather than a robot manufacturer, the association says its mission has supported robotics innovation and commercialization since 2010.
- **Public events** include networking evenings, demonstrations and industry discussions; its calendar also lists partner events, so check each organizer.
- **A concrete example:** its September 2026 report describes an Automated Happy Hour interview with Rodney Brooks and Brian Heater in Mountain View.

> **Key idea:** A robotics network is useful when it connects a specific technical question with people who have deployed something similar.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think developer community:** an event is a place to compare implementation lessons, not evidence that every attendee uses the same technology stack.
- **Practice a clear demo pitch:** state the task, show the robot’s actual behavior and name one unresolved problem before asking for feedback.
- **Compare Swiss Robotics Association** for a European industry-and-research connector; their geographic focus and participation rules differ.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the online welcome** to understand the community before browsing individual events.
2. **Read the current calendar** and choose one relevant talk or demo; verify location and registration on the organizer’s linked page.
3. **Check membership conditions separately**: the site describes free membership for California robotics companies by application or invitation, not automatic membership for overseas student teams.

## In one sentence

SiERA is ESTACA’s robotics association, combining drone automation with maker projects that join mechanics, electronics and programming.

*SiERA at the 2022 Float Lift and Fly challenge, as published by ESTACA. Source: [SiERA (ESTACA)](https://www.estaca.fr/en/campus-life/student-life/technological/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two activity areas** appear in ESTACA’s description: drones and maker projects, including robotic vehicles and a 3D printer.
- **Drone automation** includes guidance, navigation and stabilization: deciding where to go, estimating the route and keeping the aircraft steady.
- **Image processing** is another possible software task; it means extracting useful information from camera images rather than merely displaying the video.

> **Key idea:** Writing a flight algorithm is only one part of making the complete aircraft behave as intended.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think layered software:** a high-level destination depends on lower-level stabilization, just as an application depends on reliable operating-system services.
- **A concrete viewing exercise:** in the Mission 1 video, separate the intended task from the aircraft’s observable movement; list what measurements a controller would need.
- **Compare Robotium (ECAM-EPMI)** for another multidisciplinary student association; SiERA’s school page provides a particularly clear bridge from programming into aerial robotics.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the association’s UAV videos** to recognize the physical platform and the challenge context before choosing a software topic.
2. **Read ESTACA’s SiERA section** and choose one question about navigation, stabilization or integration; do not infer current hardware from old challenge footage.
3. **Use the school’s published association contact** to ask about a technical exchange or public demonstration; verify current project activity before arranging a visit.

- **Think maintainable code:** the students’ “simple is the best” philosophy connects mechanical choices with the software habit of reducing hidden complexity.

- **Compare Robotronik (Grenoble INP Phelma)** for another cup team, but note that the sponsor page’s browser title mentions Phelma incorrectly; its interview identifies ESME.

## How to engage

1. **Watch ESME’s 2025 video** to connect the association’s name with its competition work.
2. **Read the 2024 school account** and choose one subsystem whose tests could be documented for the next cohort.

- **A shared innovation environment**, the park highlights robotics and autonomous systems alongside space, aviation, advanced manufacturing and materials.
- **Its featured projects** include Swissloop transport pods, ForzaETH autonomous racing and companies applying robots to industrial operations.
- **The AGVN network** connects autonomous-ground-vehicle specialists; its July 2026 field-robotics event took place at the park’s Event Hangar.

> **Key idea:** A shared campus can connect a software experiment with the people, workshops and test problems needed to make it physical.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think integration environment:** the campus is not a single library or robot; its value lies in bringing different engineering capabilities together.
- **A concrete comparison:** contrast autonomous racing with industrial inspection; both need navigation, but their test environments and success criteria differ.
- **Compare Swissloop** as a specific student team featured by the park, and Swiss Robotics Association as a broader national network rather than a campus.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the AGVN introduction** for the park-connected mobility network; it describes collaboration, not a tutorial for building a robot.
2. **Browse the park’s project stories** and select one team whose physical problem matches a 42AI prototype.
3. **Check public event details** and contact the relevant organizer before visiting; a public showcase does not imply unrestricted workshop or test-site access.
